name: TeamStarWolf - Binance Hot-Wallet Theft October 2026 Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the Binance hot-wallet theft case study, from the June 2026 tampered installer and the September fake job process to the 29 October container deployment and theft. No source names ATT&CK ids, so every binding is the study's own reading. Score 100: Binance's own record states the behavior and the technique fits directly. Score 60: Binance's record states the behavior and the fit is the study's inference. Score 40: the behavior, or the detail the technique turns on, is known only from Reported sources. Scores measure the strength of the tie to this record, not severity. The signing-service abuse, the EIP-7702 delegations and the laundering have no ATT&CK technique and are left out. Comments carry the study's source numbers.

techniques.comment: Engineer A's role and colleague information exposed after the tampered installer (June 2026); its use to pick the September target is the study's inference. Inferred mapping. Sources: [1].
The "assignment" code repository carrying the malicious install script (September 2026); reading it as staged malware is the study's inference. Inferred mapping. Sources: [1].
Fake job process with two interview rounds (September 2026, Binance); the approach through a legitimate job platform is Chainalysis's account (3 Nov 2026), Reported. Sources: [13] [1].
Tampered Homebrew installer run (June 2026); assignment install script run (September 2026). Sources: [1] [2].
A legitimate pyenv component replaced with a malicious one, undetected by endpoint tools (September 2026). Sources: [1].
An internal AI tool used from Engineer B's machine to take control of Engineers A and C's devices (20 Oct 2026). Fits by function, not a named deployment suite. Inferred mapping. Sources: [1] [2].
An internal AI tool used from Engineer B's machine to take control of Engineers A and C's devices (20 Oct 2026). Fits by function, not a named deployment suite. Inferred mapping. Sources: [1] [2].
A token with container deployment permissions held on Engineer A's computer (20 Oct 2026); left at the parent because the record does not say where the token sat. Sources: [1].
The stolen deployment token used to deploy a container (29 Oct 2026, 17:15 to 19:56 as Binance gives it; time zone not checked). Sources: [2].
A container deployed with the stolen token, after which the hot wallet signing service was abused (29 Oct 2026). Sources: [2].

A self-destruct mechanism destroyed tooling and traces (Teng, 31 Oct 2026); traces of the initial compromise removed (Binance post-mortem as The Record relays it, 3 Nov 2026). Reported. Sources: [20] [21].
About $6.34 billion moved from Binance hot wallets on ten chains from about 20:05 UTC on 29 Oct 2026 to 23:56 UTC. Sources: [1] [3] [9].
